title: Loading & Towing
whatItIs: A heavy load or a trailer changes how your car brakes, steers and handles. Load it safely and know your limits.

keyFacts.text: Your load MUST be secure and MUST NOT stick out dangerously.
You MUST NOT overload your car or trailer: check the handbook for the maximum weights.

keyFacts: With a heavy load you may need to change the tyre pressures and headlight aim.
If a trailer or caravan starts to snake, ease off the accelerator and slow down gently.
Towing: 50 mph on single carriageways, 60 mph on dual carriageways and motorways.

a.label: Trailer snaking
points: Slow down gently, no harsh braking

b.label: Car skidding
points: Steer the way the rear is sliding

onTheTest.question: Your caravan starts to snake from side to side. What should you do?
options: Ease off the accelerator and slow down gently
onTheTest.why: Ease off the accelerator and reduce speed gently until the caravan is under control again.

traps: Speeding up doesn't cure snaking: slowing down gently does.
Towing on a motorway with 3 or more lanes: never the right-hand lane.
A load sticking out dangerously is illegal, not just risky.

review.notes: Licence towing rule: drivers who passed their car test on or after 1 January 1997 can tow trailers up to 3,500 kg MAM since 16 December 2021. Confirm on gov.uk/towing-with-car.
